title: Sherlock Alternatives: Browser Search, Setup & Limits
description: Compare MyRecon browser search with Sherlock and Maigret. See a recorded username demonstration, current access limits and how to verify public leads.
h1: Sherlock alternatives: when browser username search helps
intro: If you want a Sherlock alternative without a local installation, MyRecon provides a browser workflow for public username leads. Keep Sherlock when local commands and repeatable output matter; consider Maigret for enriched reports. MyRecon publishes this comparison. These choices describe workflows, not an independent accuracy ranking.

sections.heading: Choose for your task: MyRecon, Sherlock or Maigret
sections.body: MyRecon suits a one-off browser review or a device where you cannot install tools. Sherlock suits local command automation and output files you manage. Maigret documents enriched research reports, a web interface and library use. Each needs source review; a larger advertised catalogue cannot establish who owns a profile.

sections.heading: Current MyRecon website access limits
sections.body: Guests get 5 Quick scans daily across 100 platforms, with only the first 2 result cards visible. Signed-in free accounts get 5 Standard scans daily across 500+ platforms; Quick and Standard share that account allowance. Resets are midnight UTC (05:30 India). The optional one-time pack is ₹99 through Indian checkout or US$3.99 through an enabled international checkout, adding unlimited Standard, Deep Search and 10 Extended scans across a separate 3,000+ catalogue. Credits do not expire; nothing auto-renews. The Android app is available globally on Google Play; Android access is shown in the app. Review the linked pricing page before choosing a plan.

sections.heading: Reproduce a small browser and local review
sections.body: Choose one handle you own. In MyRecon select Quick as a guest, or sign in for Standard. For Sherlock, its official repository documents pipx install sherlock-project, followed by sherlock YOUR_HANDLE --site GitHub --csv for a bounded example; replace YOUR_HANDLE with your own handle and review --help for the installed version. Record the query, date, version, selected sites, source URL and unresolved responses. This is a reproducible procedure, not a claim that we ran a new Sherlock benchmark for this update. Sherlock --json supplies a site-data file; it is not a JSON report-export switch.

sections.heading: Real demonstration: inspect one dated measurement
sections.body: The published 30 September 2026 case used the owner-requested public handle 4ryanwalia. MyRecon checked 561 catalogue entries and Sherlock checked 430; these unequal scopes prevent a general coverage ranking. On the GitHub address, both recorded found. MyRecon also retained a Reddit challenge as unknown. Open the linked raw data for versions, check records and source observations. The example establishes how to review evidence, not account ownership or current results.

sections.heading: What to do when tools disagree
sections.body: Compare the exact public profile address, not only a brand or platform name. Open the source using ordinary permitted access. A profile-specific page can support existence; a login wall, challenge, timeout or generic success response can leave a check unknown. Retain unknowns and duplicate URLs when reviewing the raw report, then deduplicate addresses before counting leads. Confirm your own accounts through provider access and saved records before changing them.

sections.heading: When MyRecon is useful, and when another workflow fits
sections.body: Use MyRecon when you remember an old handle and want public leads to compare with your inbox or password manager. The same workflow can support an authorized footprint review, while the separate email tool checks supported breach exposure without spending the username allowance. Keep a local tool when scripting or local file control is the requirement. Neither approach reveals all private profiles, authenticates identity or deletes accounts.

sections.heading: Data handling and limits at the source
sections.body: Local Sherlock execution still sends requests to third-party sites; MyRecon uses hosted services as described in its privacy policy. Neither is automatically anonymous. Rate limits, login restrictions, changing site rules and provider outages affect what can be observed. Use bounded authorized inputs and keep exports private. A paid scan expands product scope, not your access rights on the source platform.

faq.question: Is MyRecon a free Sherlock alternative?
faq.answer: It offers free guest Quick previews and a signed-in daily Standard allowance, with optional paid features. Guest results show only the first 2 cards; see pricing for current limits.

faq.question: Does this comparison prove one tool is more accurate?
faq.answer: No. The linked historical case covers one username and unequal catalogues. It cannot establish general accuracy or current source availability.

faq.question: When is Sherlock a better fit?
faq.answer: Consider Sherlock when you need a local command-line workflow or script integration and can maintain the environment and review the sources.
